questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement $I$~: $o$-Nitrophenol is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding.

Statement $II$~: $o$-Nitrophenol has high melting point due to hydrogen bonding..

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement $I$~is true but Statement $II$& is false
Statement $I$~is false but Statement $II$& is true
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Statement I: In o-nitrophenol, the $-OH$ and $-NO_2$ groups are present at adjacent positions on the benzene ring. This close proximity allows for the formation of intramolecular hydrogen bonding. Because the hydrogen bonding is within the molecule itself, it prevents the association of different molecules. This results in weak intermolecular forces, making o-nitrophenol steam volatile. Hence, Statement I is true.

Statement II: As established, o-nitrophenol exhibits intramolecular hydrogen bonding. This prevents the formation of intermolecular hydrogen bonds, which would otherwise hold molecules tightly together in a solid lattice. Consequently, o-nitrophenol has a relatively lower melting point compared to its isomers like p-nitrophenol, which exhibit intermolecular hydrogen bonding and exist as associated molecules. Hence, Statement II is false.

Therefore, Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.q:
Order of Covalent bond;

A.& $KF > KI; LiF > KF$

B.~$KF KF$

C.~${SnCl}_{4} > {SnCl}_{2}; CuCl > NaCl$

D.~$LiF > KF; CuCl > NaCl$

E.~$KF NaCl$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
According to Fajan's Rule, small cation has more polarising power and larger anion has more polarisability. These& small cations and larger anions favours covalent character.

A.& $KF > KI-$False (Iodide is larger anion than~fluoride)

~$LiF > KF -$True (Lithium-ion is smaller cation than potassium ion)

B.~$KF < KI -$True;~$LiF > KF -$True

C.~${SnCl}_{4} > {SnCl}_{2} -$True(${Sn}^{4 +}$~is smaller than~${Sn}^{2 +}$);~

The ions with pseudo inert gas configuration prefers the covalent character.

$CuCl > NaCl -$True(${Cu}^{+} ( 3s^{2}3p^{6}3d^{10} )$~ion has pseudo inert gas configuration)

D.~$LiF > KF -$True;~$CuCl < NaCl -$False

E.~$KF < KI -$True;~$CuCl > NaCl -$True

questions.q:
The number of non-polar molecules from the following is
$HF, {H}_{2}O, {SO}_{2}, {H}_{2}, {CO}_{2}, {CH}_{4}, {NH}_{3}, HCl, {CHCl}_{3}, {BF}_{3}$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The molecules which have perfect geometry and no lone pairs are zero dipole moment molecules. Those molecules termed as non-polar molecules. Amongst the given compounds, ${CH}_{4}, {CO}_{2}, {H}_{2}, {BF}_{3}$ are non polar molecules.

${H}_{2}O$ has two lone pairs and two bond pairs. ${SO}_{2}$ has two sigma bond pairs and one lone pair. ${CHCl}_{3}$ has net dipole moment because the bond moments do not cancel with each other. ${NH}_{3}$ have one lone pair and three bond pairs. In $HF$ bond moment is the dipole moment. Hence, all these molecules have some net dipole moment.

The non-polar molecules are ${CO}_{2}, {H}_{2}, {CH}_{4}$ and ${BF}_{3}$
